title: Negation, quantity and comparison in discourse
prior_teaching_boundary: Only the fourteen active contracts and actual registers at 9129cda establish teaching. Recognition and supplied exposure are distinct from production; no archived milestones are inherited.
productive_outcomes: Express a single negative proposition with finite ne and a negative person, thing, or determiner; distinguish this negative concord from affirmative constituent contrast with nā.

Produce all twelve selected indicative positions of nabban and negative willan, and the complete twelve-position negative wesan/eom/wæs system; retain composite uncontracted expressions as their component words.
Produce the complete strong NGDA system of nān and the eight personal/neuter NGDA positions of gehwā/gehwæt in the bounded ordinary negative and distributive uses.
Distinguish an interrogative person from an indefinite person in a condition, an unnamed person introduced by ān, and the defective impersonal nominative man expression.

Build a free-choice clause using the case demanded inside that clause and an explicit resumptive pronoun when the main-clause relation differs; account for contextual subjunctive choice without treating an introductory word as an automatic mood switch.
Distinguish singular distribution from a plural total, coordinate both objects with ǣgðer ge … ge, and distinguish personal partitive uncer from the agreeing possessive.
Keep equative comparison, preferential swīðor, quantity, and proportional swā … swā distinct in meaning and structure.

Produce the independently assigned complete nominal and verbal systems with their evidenced stem alternations, ending rules, exceptions, and bounded ordinary senses; reference cells retain their separate scope.
Translate all fifty original Cook prompts with their original lexical, participant, number, mood, omission, and word-order controls, using visible help for expressly supplied dependencies.
recognition_outcomes: Identify the negative and indefinite family members explicitly retained as supplied citations, including anything/nothing, -hwega, and unused either/neither variants; do not infer unseen forms or independent productive use.
Explain case and number despite syncretic surfaces, especially root nouns, sweostor, nān, gehwā, personal uncer, and possessive uncer.
Follow the complete opening argument of Duties: withheld gifts, withdrawal of bounty, promised repayment, the embedded quotation, and the speaker's identification with the least recipients.
Follow Alfred's complete preface: two methods of translation, practical obstacles, later versification, the request to readers, and changes of pronoun referent in the final comparison.
Follow the complete prayer: grounds of entreaty, subjunctive request, successive imperatives, the two standards of comparison, purpose, the list of divine roles, and the concluding wish.
Recognize exact supported source forms and constructions while preserving their lexical, number, case, and discourse limits.
bounded_scope: The baseline is the actual fourteen active contracts and cumulative registers at 9129cda; archived-course teaching creates no prerequisite credit.
A complete morphology table does not teach every construction or sense. Productive, recognition, and supplied status is recorded independently for each form, sense, and feature.
Negative willan indicative forms do not promote the earlier supplied negative subjunctive nolde. The present negative wesan table includes both contracted and explicitly composite positions.
No nytan paradigm is introduced merely to complete a list of negative verbs: it is absent from the assigned exercises and readings.
Nān has its complete assigned strong NGDA system; instrumental and unassigned variants retain explicit reference limits. Gehwā has singular personal and neuter columns without invented plural forms.
Impersonal man is a bounded nominative singular expression. The ordinary count noun retains its earlier separate forms and sense.

The selected full noun systems distinguish productive count meanings from reference-only number positions for abstract or mass nouns. Engle and Dęne receive their documented plural systems without fabricated singular ethnonyms.

Rare ordinals, the exact fifty-two-years expression, proper-name spellings, source-specific case attraction, and exceptional reader constructions remain visibly supplied where the final inventory so records.
The Duties assignment is its complete first argument, not the full outer direct speech. The continuation on printed 160–161 is unassigned. The Preface and Prayer are complete.
All 27 original reader notes and 33 anchors remain separate from modern help. Their embedded questions become tasks only where the task plan explicitly assigns an output.
Eight short translated teaching examples have their own exact whole-sequence bindings and ungraded teaching records. No extra connected narrative or unbound worked example is included.
This proposal precedes the learning contract. Learner prose, final keys, blind learner-solving review, independent paradigm/source review, and exported-page review remain later stages.

audited_inflection_rules.description: Strong masculine: uninflected nominative/accusative singular, -es/-e; plural -as/-a/-um/-as.
Retain the vowel in the final short-stem element sceamul before endings; the long first element fōt- does not turn the final element into a heavy stem. Full uncontracted cells selected.
Heavy neuter nominative/accusative singular and plural have no ending; other endings -es/-e/-a/-um. Short final stem bebod- takes plural -u.
hēafod has the syncopated hēafd- stem before endings, with selected nominative/accusative plural hēafdu (§47.1,6).

Heavy feminine: nominative singular uninflected; oblique singular -e; plural -a/-a/-um/-a. -nes doubles s before endings. Abstract -ung/-ing has the same selected endings; -a oblique singular variants remain recognition alternatives.
Weak masculine: -a nominative singular, -an other singular and nominative/accusative plural, -ena genitive plural, -um dative plural.
tōð follows fōt: dative singular and nominative/accusative plural tēð, genitive singular tōðes, plural genitive tōða and dative tōðum. Cook also admits tōðe and tōðas.

bōc: genitive/dative singular and nominative/accusative plural bēc; genitive plural bōca, dative plural bōcum. Genitive singular bōce follows the explicitly admitted regular -e genitive alternative for this class.
sweostor is unchanged throughout the singular and nominative/accusative plural, with genitive plural sweostra and dative plural sweostrum; no invented umlaut.

Selected people names Engle and Dęne have plural-only lexical scope: -e nominative/accusative, -a genitive, -um dative. Dęniga/Dęnia genitive plural variants are explicit in §44.2; do not manufacture a singular by backformation.
Agent noun in -end: selected plural nominative/accusative zero, genitive -ra, dative -um. Cook admits nominative/accusative plural -e and -as variants.

Complete singular selection hǣtu/hǣte and invariant hǣlu; -u/-o/-e oblique variation is recognized. Wright184 §§382–383 explicitly lists both under strengu and warns few such nouns have plurals. BT500b lists hǣlu indeclinable. No plural lexical use assigned.

Wright184 prints the complete strengu class model: singular nominative strengu/-o, accusative/genitive/dative strenge/-u/-o; plural nominative/accusative strenga/-e/-u/-o, genitive strenga and dative strengum. Select one explicit eight-cell reference column without assigning an independently productive count sense. Earlier ðīestru taught only plural forms and does not establish this complete class.

audited_inflection_rules.statement: Ne precedes a finite verb. The selected negative copula combines uncontracted ne eom/ne eart/ne sindon with nis and the contracted preterite næs/nǣre/nǣron. These alternatives form one complete twelve-position indicative construction table. An uncontracted cell contains two existing words, not a new multiword inflected verb. Negative willan selects Cook’s e-vowel alternatives nelle/nelt/nele/nellað and nolde/noldest/noldon. Other spellings are valid source variants, not extra selected recall targets.

Cook’s habban table and ne+h contraction (§29), with the already checked Unit2 negative cells, give næbbe, næfst, næfð, nabbað; preterite næfde, næfdest, næfde, næfdon. The negative cells are rule-derived, not separately printed in a full negative table. Do not conflate first-singular bb with other singular f. Retain the earlier form identities and recognition histories.

Nān follows strong long-stem adjective NGDA endings, with nominative/accusative neuter plural nān and feminine plural nāna, masculine accusative singular nānne. Long ā remains. No invented weak system or general negative spelling rule.
Gehwā compounds the singular interrogative hwā/hwæt. Select prior gehwǣm (not silently substitute hwām). Accusative persons gehwone versus things gehwæt. No distinct feminine morphology or plural.
The selected adverb has swīðe, swīðor, swīðost, with unchanged long ī. The comparative can mark preference with ðonne; the two compared objects retain their governed case.

StrongIII forgieldan has present gield-, past singular geald-, plural guld-, participle gold-. Present2/3 forgieltst/forgielt continue the earlier gieldan selected t cluster. Tōweorpan has weorp-/wearp-/wurp-/worpen; its present2/3 uses umlaut wierp-. Past2singular uses the plural stem plus -e. Singular1/3past bare stem; all pastpl -on. All presentpl -að. Prefixes stay with all stems.

Ongietan follows gietan/giefan classV: ongiet-/ongeat-/ongēat-/ongieten. Present2 ongietst and3 ongiett keep selected t+t assimilation (Cook prints giet(t)); the alternative single t is valid but not the selected cell. Preterite2 uses ongēate, other singular ongeat, plural ongēaton. The infinitive and participle in the principal-parts display are reference only.

Gehātan follows the prior hātan selected system with ge-: gehāte/gehǣtst/gehǣtt/gehātað; past gehēt/gehēte/gehēton. The ā→ǣ present2/3 and ēpast are both required. Onfōn keeps the contract infinitives onfōn/onfōnne; forlǣtan keeps forlǣtan/forlǣtanne. No negative or subjunctive prefixed system is inferred.

Standan is classVI, not classIII: standan/stōd/stōdon/standen. Its present base standende keeps the nasal in the present stem; past standen is the selected fourth principal part. Only the participial base pair is newly promoted.

Selected long-stem weakI wēnan,lǣran,forbærnan use present -e,-st,-ð,-að and preterite -de,-dest,-de,-don. Selected participial bases lǣrende/lǣred and hǣlende/hǣled retain full -ed; the frame does not license arbitrary syncopation. Imperative singular has no ending (ætīew, ālīes); plural -að. Plain/inflected wyrcean/wyrceanne preserve earlier selected -ea- before the infinitival ending, rather than silently substituting wyrcan.

Weak II hȳrian follows lufian: present hȳrie, hȳrast, hȳrað, hȳriað; preterite hȳrode, hȳrodest, hȳrode, hȳrodon. The long ȳ is lexical and stays throughout. Commands cleopa/cleopiað distinguish singular -a from plural -iað. The selected pair is blōstmian/blōstmianne; no finite system is assigned.

Riht and gelīc use ordinary long-stem positive adjective NGDA endings. Zero nominative feminine singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural; strong feminine plural -a selected, masculine -e; weak genitive plural -ra. Long ī in gelīc stays.

Mǣre is Cook§59: retain citation -e where no ending is supplied; drop it before another ending, including selected feminine nominative singular mǣru and neuter nominative/accusative plural mǣru. Strong -re/-ra with stem-final r contracts to mǣrre/mǣrra. Weak genitive plural mǣrra.

Mihtig follows the disyllabic -ig pattern (§57.3): the selected table syncopates i before vowel-initial endings (mihtges, mihtgum, mihtge, mihtgan); retains i before consonantal endings (mihtigne, mihtigre, mihtigra). Select mihtig for strong feminine nominative singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural, parallel to the established hālig pattern. Unsyncopated variants must not be called impossible.

Ungeðancfull is explicitly Cook§58.2: retain final ll before vowels (ungeðancfulle, -fullum), but select one l before consonants (ungeðancfulne, -fulre, -fulra). Bare ungeðancfull keeps the lexical double consonant.

local_support.text: The two superlative adverbs mean “most clearly and most intelligibly.” For plus dative introduces the worldly cares that constrained how clearly Alfred could explain it. local_support.text: Hæfde underfangen = “had received/taken charge of.” The repeated hæfde governs both geleornod and gewęnd: “had studied ... and translated ...”. local_support.text: Supply hē (Alfred) with bitt and hālsað, as Cook’s note4 directs. Ǣlcne ðāra ðe ... means “each of those who ...”. local_support.text: The two superlative adverbs mean “most clearly and most intelligibly.” For plus dative introduces the worldly cares that constrained how clearly Alfred could explain it. Ǣgðer ge ... ge means “both ... and.” On mōde/on līchaman identify mind and body. Sind is the plural present “are.” The relative ðe at word61 refers to bisga; those cares are the subject of becōmon.

local_support.text: Hæfde underfangen = “had received/taken charge of.” The repeated hæfde governs both geleornod and gewęnd: “had studied ... and translated ...”. local_support.text: Ælfred is subject. The feminine hīe/hēo refers to bōc. The source-language phrases use of plus dative; on Englisc gives the translation’s goal. Word be worde contrasts literal verbal correspondence with andgiet of andgiete, sense for sense. Gedōn describes the work’s resulting arrangement.

local_support.text: The two superlative adverbs mean “most clearly and most intelligibly.” For plus dative introduces the worldly cares that constrained how clearly Alfred could explain it. Ǣgðer ge ... ge means “both ... and.” On mōde/on līchaman identify mind and body. Sind is the plural present “are.” The relative ðe at word61 refers to bisga; those cares are the subject of becōmon.
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source

local_support.text: Hæfde underfangen = “had received/taken charge of.” The repeated hæfde governs both geleornod and gewęnd: “had studied ... and translated ...”. Ðēah here is “nevertheless”; ðā ... ðā frames “when ... then.” Tō Engliscum spelle and tō lēoðe mark resulting literary form. Hīe/hēo still refers to the book.

local_support.text: Supply hē (Alfred) with bitt and hālsað, as Cook’s note4 directs. Ǣlcne ðāra ðe ... means “each of those who ...”. Lyste is impersonal: “whom it may please to read this book”; its understood accusative experiencer is the prospective reader. The requested ðæt clause contains subjunctive gebidde, “that he pray for him.”

local_support.text: Ne wīte continues the request: “and not blame him.” In gif hē hit rihtlicor ongiete ðonne hē meahte, the first hē is the reader and the second is Alfred (Cook’s notes6–7). Ongiete is subjunctive; wīte is the verb “blame,” not the noun “punishment.”

local_support.text: The two superlative adverbs mean “most clearly and most intelligibly.” For plus dative introduces the worldly cares that constrained how clearly Alfred could explain it. local_support.text: Dryhten and God are direct address; ælmihtiga is weak singular. Wyrhta and Wealdend are “Maker and Ruler,” with genitive ealra gesceafta. This Maker sense is distinct from the previously taught workman sense.

local_support.text: The for phrases name grounds of appeal. In ðǣre hālgan rōde tācne, the genitive phrase “of the holy cross” depends on dative tācne. Sanctæ Marian and Sancti Michaeles are supplied names in genitive function with mixed foreign-name inflection; do not derive a new productive Latin paradigm. Gehīersumnesse is obedience. Hālgena means saints; lufan is the weak noun’s dative; earnungum means merits.

local_support.text: The requested ðæt clause has gewissie, “that you guide.” Bęt ðonne ic āworhte tō ðē means better than my conduct towards you has deserved. The following gewissa is a direct singular command. In mīnre sāwle ðearfe, mīnre sāwle is genitive, dependent on dative ðearfe: “for my soul’s benefit.” Cunne is first-singular subjunctive, “than I myself may know.”

local_support.text: Gestaðela, gestranga, āfierr and gescield are addressed singular commands. Establish my mind according to your will; strengthen me against the devil’s temptations; remove lust and unrighteousness; protect me against visible and invisible adversaries. The latter adjectives agree with dative plural wiðerwinnum.

local_support.text: Tǣc takes dative mē. Its following ðīnne willan is the accusative object of wyrceanne (“to do your will”), as Cook’s note7 specifies. The ðæt clause gives purpose with mæge. Tōforan eallum ðingum means above all things; the two mid phrases give manner: with pure thought and a pure body.

local_support.text: The for phrases name grounds of appeal. In ðǣre hālgan rōde tācne, the genitive phrase “of the holy cross” depends on dative tācne. Sanctæ Marian and Sancti Michaeles are supplied names in genitive function with mixed foreign-name inflection; do not derive a new productive Latin paradigm. Gehīersumnesse is obedience. Hālgena means saints; lufan is the weak noun’s dative; earnungum means merits.

local_support.text: The requested ðæt clause has gewissie, “that you guide.” Bęt ðonne ic āworhte tō ðē means better than my conduct towards you has deserved. The following gewissa is a direct singular command. In mīnre sāwle ðearfe, mīnre sāwle is genitive, dependent on dative ðearfe: “for my soul’s benefit.” Cunne is first-singular subjunctive, “than I myself may know.”

local_support.text: Gestaðela, gestranga, āfierr and gescield are addressed singular commands. local_support.text: The for phrases name grounds of appeal. In ðǣre hālgan rōde tācne, the genitive phrase “of the holy cross” depends on dative tācne. local_support.text: The requested ðæt clause has gewissie, “that you guide.” Bęt ðonne ic āworhte tō ðē means better than my conduct towards you has deserved. local_support.text: Use him mid hundtēontigum forgolden bið, “he will be repaid a hundredfold,” with the finite verb last. The initial ǣlc has its own relative clause and is resumed by dative him; this is an impersonal recipient-passive scaffold. Mid hundtēontigum is taken from the checked Duties paragraph, then adapted to this passive. For mīnum naman means for the sake of my name. Neither the numeral phrase nor this resumed construction is a new general production system.

local_support.title: A promise to whichever son
local_support.text: Use Engliscra lēoða, of English poems. The supported recipient expression is swā hwæðrum hiere twēgra suna swā hīe ǣrest leornode. Hwæðrum is dative singular because the whole expression is the recipient of promising, while its understood referent is the learner in the subordinate clause. This case attraction is supplied, not a general production target. Leornode here is prospective preterite subjunctive, identical in spelling to the indicative; it does not claim that he had already learned the book. Original independent free-choice exercises use nominative hwæðer and an explicit resumptive dative.

source_spans.selection_rationale: Complete first argumentative paragraph: rebuke for withholding goods, the giver’s future response, and a gospel promise of repayment. The outer speech continues in the following distinct rebuke; this is not the complete speech or complete Reader IX.
source_spans.unassigned_continuation: Printed160.1 through Reader IX ending161.20; the next paragraph begins Ðū mann, tō hwon eart ðū mē swā ungeðancfull.
source_spans.origin_category: exact source; layout and note-marker removal declared

source_lines.source_with_note_markers: Se Hǣlend cwæð tō ðǣm wlancan[1]: “For hwȳ wǣre
ðū swā fæsthafol mīnra gōda, ðe ic ðē sealde? Tō
hwon[2] rēcelēasodest ðū ðǣre giefe, ðe ic ðē geaf? Ic ðē
nū āfierre[3] fram mīnre sęlene, ðe ic ðē forgeaf; ðonne
bist[3] ðū wǣdla on woruldlīfe. For hwon[2] noldest[4] ðū
geðęncean ðæt ic wille[5] forgieldan ǣghwilcum męnn āne
gōde dǣd, ðe for mīnum naman mann gedēð? Mid
hundtēontigum ic hit him forgielde,[3] swā hit is on
mīnum godspelle gecweden and gesǣd,[6] ‘Swā-hwæt-swā[7]
gē sęllað ānum of mīnum ðǣm lǣstum,[8] gē hit simle mē
sęllað,[9] and ic ēow wið[10] ðǣm gesęlle[3] ēcne drēam[11] on
heofonum.’

source_spans.learner_text: Se Hǣlend cwæð tō ðǣm wlancan: “For hwȳ wǣre ðū swā fæsthafol mīnra gōda, ðe ic ðē sealde? Tō hwon rēcelēasodest ðū ðǣre giefe, ðe ic ðē geaf? Ic ðē nū āfierre fram mīnre sęlene, ðe ic ðē forgeaf; ðonne bist ðū wǣdla on woruldlīfe. For hwon noldest ðū geðęncean ðæt ic wille forgieldan ǣghwilcum męnn āne gōde dǣd, ðe for mīnum naman mann gedēð? Mid hundtēontigum ic hit him forgielde, swā hit is on mīnum godspelle gecweden and gesǣd, ‘Swā-hwæt-swā gē sęllað ānum of mīnum ðǣm lǣstum, gē hit simle mē sęllað, and ic ēow wið ðǣm gesęlle ēcne drēam on heofonum.’

local_support.text: For hwȳ and tō hwon ask why. Fæsthafol governs the genitive mīnra gōda, “holding tightly to my goods”; rēcelēasodest takes genitive ðǣre giefe, “neglected the gift.” Relative ðe introduces the following clauses; long ðē is the personal pronoun “you/to you.”

local_support.text: Āfierre, bist, forgielde and gesęlle have present morphology with future reference in this promised response. Noldest is “you would not/refused”; geðęncean is its infinitive. Wille expresses the present speaker’s intention even within a remembered proposition: no mechanical backshift is required.

local_support.text: Ǣghwilcum męnn is the dative recipient; āne gōde dǣd is the accusative object. The subject of gedēð is generic mann, “one/a person.” Mid hundtēontigum means “with a hundredfold.” The singular him refers back to the person.

local_support.text: Gecweden and gesǣd are two past participles with is; Cook calls the pairing pleonastic. Swā-hwæt-swā means “whatever,” the object of sęllað. Ānum of mīnum ðǣm lǣstum means “to one of my least ones”; lǣstum is substantival and dative plural. The repeated gē/sęllað address the quoted audience.

local_support.text: Wið ðǣm means “in return for that,” with dative singular. Drēam here means joy or bliss, not a dream. Ēcne agrees with accusative masculine drēam.

source_lines.source_with_note_markers: Ælfred cyning wæs wealhstōd[1] ðisse bēc, and hīe of
Bōclædene[2] on Englisc węnde, swā hēo nū is gedōn.
Hwīlum hē sętte word be worde, hwīlum andgiet of
andgiete, swā-swā hē hit ðā sweotolost and andgiet-
fullicost geręccan meahte for ðǣm mislicum and manig-
fealdum woruldbisgum ðe hine oft ǣgðer ge on mōde
ge on līchaman bisgodon. Ðā bisga[3] ūs sind swīðe
earfoðrīme ðe on his dagum on ðā rīcu becōmon ðe hē
underfangen hæfde, and ðēah, ðā hē ðās bōc hæfde
geleornod, and of Lædene tō Engliscum spelle gewęnd,
ðā geworhte hē hīe eft tō lēoðe, swā-swā hēo nū gedōn
is. And nū bitt[4] and for Godes naman hālsað ǣlcne
ðāra ðe ðās bōc rǣdan lyste,[5] ðæt hē for hine gebidde,
and him ne wīte gif hē[6] hit rihtlicor ongiete ðonne hē[7]
meahte; for-ðām-ðe ǣlc mann sceal be his andgietes
mǣðe, and be his ǣmettan, sprecan ðæt hē spricð, and
dōn ðæt-ðæt hē dēð.

local_support.text: Ælfred is subject. The feminine hīe/hēo refers to bōc. The source-language phrases use of plus dative; on Englisc gives the translation’s goal. Word be worde contrasts literal verbal correspondence with andgiet of andgiete, sense for sense. Gedōn describes the work’s resulting arrangement.
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source
local_support.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

local_support.text: The two superlative adverbs mean “most clearly and most intelligibly.” For plus dative introduces the worldly cares that constrained how clearly Alfred could explain it. Ǣgðer ge ... ge means “both ... and.” On mōde/on līchaman identify mind and body. Sind is the plural present “are.” The relative ðe at word61 refers to bisga; those cares are the subject of becōmon.
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source

local_support.text: Hæfde underfangen = “had received/taken charge of.” The repeated hæfde governs both geleornod and gewęnd: “had studied ... and translated ...”. Ðēah here is “nevertheless”; ðā ... ðā frames “when ... then.” Tō Engliscum spelle and tō lēoðe mark resulting literary form. Hīe/hēo still refers to the book.
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source
local_support.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

local_support.text: Supply hē (Alfred) with bitt and hālsað, as Cook’s note4 directs. Ǣlcne ðāra ðe ... means “each of those who ...”. Lyste is impersonal: “whom it may please to read this book”; its understood accusative experiencer is the prospective reader. The requested ðæt clause contains subjunctive gebidde, “that he pray for him.”

local_support.text: Ne wīte continues the request: “and not blame him.” In gif hē hit rihtlicor ongiete ðonne hē meahte, the first hē is the reader and the second is Alfred (Cook’s notes6–7). Ongiete is subjunctive; wīte is the verb “blame,” not the noun “punishment.”

local_support.text: Be ... mǣðe and be ... ǣmettan mean according to the measure of one’s understanding and one’s available leisure. Sceal governs sprecan and dōn. Both ðæt ... and ðæt-ðæt ... function as “what/that which.” Preserve the source’s hyphenated spelling in the latter.

source_lines.source_with_note_markers: Dryhten,[1] ælmihtiga God,[1] Wyrhta and Wealdend ealra
gesceafta, ic bidde ðē for ðīnre miclan mildheortnesse,
and for ðǣre hālgan rōde tācne,[2] and for Sanctæ Marian
mægðhāde, and for Sancti Michaeles gehīersumnesse, and
for ealra ðīnra hālgena[3] lufan and hīera earnungum, ðæt
ðū mē gewissie[4] bęt ðonne ic āworhte tō ðē; and gewissa
mē tō ðīnum willan, and tō mīnre sāwle ðearfe,[5] bęt ðonne
ic self cunne[6]; and gestaðela mīn mōd tō ðīnum willan and
tō mīnre sāwle ðearfe; and gestranga mē wið ðæs dēofles[3]
costnungum; and āfierr fram mē ðā fūlan gālnesse and ǣlce
unrihtwīsnesse; and gescield mē wið mīnum wiðerwinnum,
gesewenlicum and ungesewenlicum; and tǣc mē ðīnne will-
an[7] tō wyrceanne; ðæt ic mæge[8] ðē inweardlīce lufian tō-
foran eallum ðingum, mid clǣnum geðance and mid clǣnum
līchaman. For-ðon-ðe ðū eart mīn Scieppend,[9] and mīn
Ālīesend, mīn Fultum, mīn Frōfor, mīn Trēownes, and
mīn Tōhopa. Sīe ðē lof and wuldor nū and ā ā ā, tō
worulde būtan ǣghwilcum ęnde. Amen.

source_spans.learner_text: Dryhten, ælmihtiga God, Wyrhta and Wealdend ealra gesceafta, ic bidde ðē for ðīnre miclan mildheortnesse, and for ðǣre hālgan rōde tācne, and for Sanctæ Marian mægðhāde, and for Sancti Michaeles gehīersumnesse, and for ealra ðīnra hālgena lufan and hīera earnungum, ðæt ðū mē gewissie bęt ðonne ic āworhte tō ðē; and gewissa mē tō ðīnum willan, and tō mīnre sāwle ðearfe, bęt ðonne ic self cunne; and gestaðela mīn mōd tō ðīnum willan and tō mīnre sāwle ðearfe; and gestranga mē wið ðæs dēofles costnungum; and āfierr fram mē ðā fūlan gālnesse and ǣlce unrihtwīsnesse; and gescield mē wið mīnum wiðerwinnum, gesewenlicum and ungesewenlicum; and tǣc mē ðīnne willan tō wyrceanne; ðæt ic mæge ðē inweardlīce lufian tōforan eallum ðingum, mid clǣnum geðance and mid clǣnum līchaman. For-ðon-ðe ðū eart mīn Scieppend, and mīn Ālīesend, mīn Fultum, mīn Frōfor, mīn Trēownes, and mīn Tōhopa. Sīe ðē lof and wuldor nū and ā ā ā, tō worulde būtan ǣghwilcum ęnde. Amen.

local_support.text: Dryhten and God are direct address; ælmihtiga is weak singular. Wyrhta and Wealdend are “Maker and Ruler,” with genitive ealra gesceafta. This Maker sense is distinct from the previously taught workman sense.
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source
local_support.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

local_support.text: The for phrases name grounds of appeal. In ðǣre hālgan rōde tācne, the genitive phrase “of the holy cross” depends on dative tācne. Sanctæ Marian and Sancti Michaeles are supplied names in genitive function with mixed foreign-name inflection; do not derive a new productive Latin paradigm. Gehīersumnesse is obedience. Hālgena means saints; lufan is the weak noun’s dative; earnungum means merits.
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source
local_support.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

local_support.text: The requested ðæt clause has gewissie, “that you guide.” Bęt ðonne ic āworhte tō ðē means better than my conduct towards you has deserved. The following gewissa is a direct singular command. In mīnre sāwle ðearfe, mīnre sāwle is genitive, dependent on dative ðearfe: “for my soul’s benefit.” Cunne is first-singular subjunctive, “than I myself may know.”
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source
local_support.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

local_support.text: Gestaðela, gestranga, āfierr and gescield are addressed singular commands. Establish my mind according to your will; strengthen me against the devil’s temptations; remove lust and unrighteousness; protect me against visible and invisible adversaries. The latter adjectives agree with dative plural wiðerwinnum.
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source
local_support.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

local_support.text: Tǣc takes dative mē. Its following ðīnne willan is the accusative object of wyrceanne (“to do your will”), as Cook’s note7 specifies. The ðæt clause gives purpose with mæge. Tōforan eallum ðingum means above all things; the two mid phrases give manner: with pure thought and a pure body.
local_support.origin_category: new teaching material explaining exact source
local_support.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

local_support.text: The final causal clause names God as Creator, Redeemer, help, comfort, trust and hope. Sīe is an optative wish, “may there be”; ðē is dative. Ā is repeated three times, followed by tō worulde būtan ǣghwilcum ęnde, “for ever without any end.”

teaching_records.scope_note: The negative determiner and finite ne express one denial.

teaching_records.text: Se mann ne hæfð męte; se mann næfð męte.
teaching_records.translation: The man does not have food; the man does not have food.
teaching_records.scope_note: The two clauses have the same negative meaning. The second uses the selected contracted finite form.
Hwā asks for the person; this is an ordinary direct question.

teaching_records.text: Gif hwā gā, hē gesiehð ðæt hūs.
teaching_records.translation: If anyone goes, he will see that house.
teaching_records.scope_note: Hwā is indefinite in the contingent condition. Gā is third-singular present subjunctive here; the following present states the prospective result.
Singular mann and hæfð express distribution to each individual.

teaching_records.text: Se cyning ānum ðissa manna bōc sęlð.
teaching_records.translation: The king gives a book to one of these men.
teaching_records.scope_note: The selected recipient is dative ānum; the group is genitive ðissa manna. The book is the accusative thing given.

teaching_records.text: Swā se cyning ieldra is, swā hē wīsra is.
teaching_records.translation: The older the king is, the wiser he is.
teaching_records.scope_note: The paired clauses correlate degrees. Each comparative agrees with the subject of its own clause.

teaching_records.text: Ne sęle ðǣm cyninge ðā bōc.
teaching_records.translation: Do not give the book to the king.
teaching_records.scope_note: Ne negates a singular command. The king remains the dative recipient and the book the accusative thing.

teaching_records.text: Ælfred is subject. The feminine hīe/hēo refers to bōc. The source-language phrases use of plus dative; on Englisc gives the translation’s goal. Word be worde contrasts literal verbal correspondence with andgiet of andgiete, sense for sense. Gedōn describes the work’s resulting arrangement.

teaching_records.text: The two superlative adverbs mean “most clearly and most intelligibly.” For plus dative introduces the worldly cares that constrained how clearly Alfred could explain it. Ǣgðer ge ... ge means “both ... and.” On mōde/on līchaman identify mind and body. Sind is the plural present “are.” The relative ðe at word61 refers to bisga; those cares are the subject of becōmon.

teaching_records.text: Hæfde underfangen = “had received/taken charge of.” The repeated hæfde governs both geleornod and gewęnd: “had studied ... and translated ...”. Ðēah here is “nevertheless”; ðā ... ðā frames “when ... then.” Tō Engliscum spelle and tō lēoðe mark resulting literary form. Hīe/hēo still refers to the book.

teaching_records.text: Supply hē (Alfred) with bitt and hālsað, as Cook’s note4 directs. Ǣlcne ðāra ðe ... means “each of those who ...”. The requested ðæt clause contains subjunctive gebidde, “that he pray for him.”

teaching_records.text: The for phrases name grounds of appeal. In ðǣre hālgan rōde tācne, the genitive phrase “of the holy cross” depends on dative tācne. Sanctæ Marian and Sancti Michaeles are supplied names in genitive function with mixed foreign-name inflection; do not derive a new productive Latin paradigm. Gehīersumnesse is obedience. Hālgena means saints; lufan is the weak noun’s dative; earnungum means merits.

teaching_records.text: The requested ðæt clause has gewissie, “that you guide.” Bęt ðonne ic āworhte tō ðē means better than my conduct towards you has deserved. The following gewissa is a direct singular command. In mīnre sāwle ðearfe, mīnre sāwle is genitive, dependent on dative ðearfe: “for my soul’s benefit.” Cunne is first-singular subjunctive, “than I myself may know.”

teaching_records.text: Gestaðela, gestranga, āfierr and gescield are addressed singular commands. Establish my mind according to your will; strengthen me against the devil’s temptations; remove lust and unrighteousness; protect me against visible and invisible adversaries. The latter adjectives agree with dative plural wiðerwinnum.

teaching_records.text: Tǣc takes dative mē. Its following ðīnne willan is the accusative object of wyrceanne (“to do your will”), as Cook’s note7 specifies. The ðæt clause gives purpose with mæge. Tōforan eallum ðingum means above all things; the two mid phrases give manner: with pure thought and a pure body.

teaching_records.title: A hundredfold requital
teaching_records.text: Use him mid hundtēontigum forgolden bið, “he will be repaid a hundredfold,” with the finite verb last. The initial ǣlc has its own relative clause and is resumed by dative him; this is an impersonal recipient-passive scaffold. Mid hundtēontigum is taken from the checked Duties paragraph, then adapted to this passive. For mīnum naman means for the sake of my name. Neither the numeral phrase nor this resumed construction is a new general production system.

teaching_records.title: The resumed subject and one of a set
teaching_records.text: Cook’s emphatic resumed sē is the supplied long-vowel nominative masculine singular. In ān of ðissum lǣstum bebodum, of+dative selects one from the set. The same long sē may be retained in30.6.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: In old times
teaching_records.text: On ealdum tīdum means in old times: temporal on takes the dative plural here. This exact supplied temporal expression is distinct from locating an object in a place.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.text: The printed word is earth, not oath. There is no source emendation.
teaching_records.origin_category: new teaching material
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.text: Either prior gedeorf labor with an explicitly licensed from relation or the source’s æt ðīnum gewinne frame requires its own final grammar binding. Reader161.5 and note6 directly support æt = from; this is evidence outside the assigned reading span.
teaching_records.origin_category: new teaching material
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: Proceeds and an omitted infinitive
teaching_records.text: Use æt his gewinne for from his labour. In ðæt hē mæg, what he can, a recoverable action such as obtain is left unexpressed. Cook159–161’s argument supplies the actual æt…gewinne…mæge construction; do not add a new independent ellipsis rule or infer a full gewinn paradigm.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.text: Brȳd is feminine; selected accsg brȳde follows Cook51b. Hām here is a noun with accusative object function, distinct from prior adverb hām homewards. Preserve the printed blōstmian hint, matching the selected blossom lemma.
teaching_records.origin_category: new teaching material
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: Let them live
teaching_records.text: Use lǣt hīe libban, let them live: the accusative hīe is the understood subject of libban. This whole permission construction is scaffolded. Gif hīe magon expresses ability, not unwillingness; a defensible third-person optative translation is also valid language.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.text: Ālīesend is productive as the singular Redeemer title. Its plural morphology is reference only and does not assign a theological plural sense.
teaching_records.origin_category: new teaching material
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: A person taught to do something
teaching_records.text: Use hē wæs lǣred … tō dōnne. The taught person is the subject of the passive and the understood agent of doing. The infinitive’s object Godes willan stays accusative, with Godes genitive. This controlled infinitive frame is supplied.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: From evil
teaching_records.text: Use fram yfele, from evil. Here yfele is the dative singular of the substantive noun yfel (Cook’s noun§47 entry), not the ordinary adjective dative yfelum; the exact phrase is supplied.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: May it come about
teaching_records.text: Use Geweorðe first, as Cook specifies: it is the supplied third-singular present subjunctive of the prefixed verb. Swā-swā means just as; retain the supplied hyphenated source expression.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: Names and the glossary Latin spelling
teaching_records.text: The proper names Ælfred, Osburg, Æthelwulf and Asser are supplied; Ælfredes is the genitive needed in31.14. Lǣdene follows the selected glossary’s Lǣden; the actual Preface reading retains its printed Lædene without a long mark. No silent change to that source reading is made.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.text: Dęne and Engle have complete plural-only lexical scope. Lēoðwyrhta is a weak masculine poet; āwęndednes is the -nes translation noun, with doubled ss in inflected forms. Lædene is a supplied dative language name.
teaching_records.origin_category: new teaching material
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: Hight
teaching_records.text: Hātte means is/was called, with past time supplied by the context. It is a special passive naming form, not the ordinary active preterite hēt. Use it unchanged in this supported sentence.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: Fifty-two years
teaching_records.text: Use twā and fīftig gēara. The already taught two is combined with supplied fīftig; the numeral expression may govern genitive plural gēara. This one number phrase is supplied, not the full higher-numeral system.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.text: Bēcrǣding was earlier supplied only; it now has a complete table with productive singular reading and reference-only plurals. The twelve-years-old phrase remains explicitly bounded higher-number syntax.
teaching_records.origin_category: new teaching material
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: After twelve years of age
teaching_records.text: Use æfter ðǣm ðe … wæs for after he was…. In twęlf wintra eald, twelve years old, wintra is genitive plural with the numeral and adjective of age. This finite after-clause and age phrase are supplied; twęlf preserves the earlier selected form. Treat ðe here as the supplied clause marker within the whole after-conjunction; it has no separate subject/object role inside the following clause.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.text: Bōc has bēc in genitive/dative singular and nominative/accusative plural; bōc remains accusative singular. Lēoða is genitive plural poems. Do not make the supplied whichever-of-two clause a blanket productive case-attraction rule.
teaching_records.origin_category: new teaching material
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: A promise to whichever son
teaching_records.text: Use Engliscra lēoða, of English poems. The supported recipient expression is swā hwæðrum hiere twēgra suna swā hīe ǣrest leornode. Hwæðrum is dative singular because the whole expression is the recipient of promising, while its understood referent is the learner in the subordinate clause. This case attraction is supplied, not a general production target. Leornode here is prospective preterite subjunctive, identical in spelling to the indicative; it does not claim that he had already learned the book. Original independent free-choice exercises use nominative hwæðer and an explicit resumptive dative.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact help visible beside every assigned task and during its assessment; no independent recall of supplied material is tested.

teaching_records.title: Giving to a recipient without an expressed subject
teaching_records.text: Use the supplied frame ēow bið giefen, “it will be given to you (plural).” Ēow is the dative recipient; no hit is expressed. For one addressee, use ðē bið giefen with a singular command. Keep the frame available while composing; its independent recall is not required.
teaching_records.origin_category: new teaching material
teaching_records.evidence_basis: Bounded new composition using the taught passive formation, dative recipient (Cook §164.a), implicit subject discussion (§190), and Cook29.9’s explicit omission instruction; not a claim that the whole model is an exact quoted Old English source sentence.
teaching_records.display_obligation: Keep this exact construction help visible beside the assigned task and throughout assessment; do not require unaided recall.

new_material_examples.pedagogical_purpose: The negative determiner and finite ne express one denial.
new_material_examples.display_obligation: Print the complete Old English example with its translation and the bounded explanatory point. The translation is teaching support, not an answer to a later identical composition.

new_material_examples.text: Se mann ne hæfð męte; se mann næfð męte.
new_material_examples.translation: The man does not have food; the man does not have food.
new_material_examples.pedagogical_purpose: The two clauses have the same negative meaning. The second uses the selected contracted finite form.

new_material_examples.text: Gif hwā gā, hē gesiehð ðæt hūs.
new_material_examples.translation: If anyone goes, he will see that house.
new_material_examples.pedagogical_purpose: Hwā is indefinite in the contingent condition. Gā is third-singular present subjunctive here; the following present states the prospective result.

new_material_examples.text: Se cyning ānum ðissa manna bōc sęlð.
new_material_examples.translation: The king gives a book to one of these men.
new_material_examples.pedagogical_purpose: The selected recipient is dative ānum; the group is genitive ðissa manna. The book is the accusative thing given.
new_material_examples.display_obligation: Print the complete Old English example with its translation and the bounded explanatory point. The translation is teaching support, not an answer to a later identical composition.

new_material_examples.text: Swā se cyning ieldra is, swā hē wīsra is.
new_material_examples.translation: The older the king is, the wiser he is.
new_material_examples.pedagogical_purpose: The paired clauses correlate degrees. Each comparative agrees with the subject of its own clause.
new_material_examples.display_obligation: Print the complete Old English example with its translation and the bounded explanatory point. The translation is teaching support, not an answer to a later identical composition.
new_material_examples.independent_grammar_review: Grammarworker confirmed the eight proposed examples linguistically sound; exact bindings remain subject to record reconciliation.

new_material_examples.text: Ne sęle ðǣm cyninge ðā bōc.
new_material_examples.translation: Do not give the book to the king.
new_material_examples.pedagogical_purpose: Ne negates a singular command. The king remains the dative recipient and the book the accusative thing.

grammar_inventory.scope_note: Wið+dative expresses payment/return: wið his dæges weorce; wið ānum pęninge. This is distinct from the prior hostile combat use.

grammar_inventory.title: Pay or requite
grammar_inventory.description: Forgieldan: recipient dative, paid thing accusative. A passive with retained recipient dative is locally scaffolded in28.1.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Forgieldan: recipient dative, paid thing accusative. A passive with retained recipient dative is locally scaffolded in28.1.

grammar_inventory.title: Suppose a proposition
grammar_inventory.description: Wēnan introduces a ðæt-content clause. In this past report sceolden expresses what the workers expected to receive; it is not automatically an obligation.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Wēnan introduces a ðæt-content clause. In this past report sceolden expresses what the workers expected to receive; it is not automatically an obligation.

grammar_inventory.title: Exact equality of amount
grammar_inventory.description: Eall can strengthen the equative: eall swā micel swā, just as much as. Micel is substantive neuter; the second recipient remains dative under the understood giving verb.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Eall can strengthen the equative: eall swā micel swā, just as much as. Micel is substantive neuter; the second recipient remains dative under the understood giving verb.

grammar_inventory.title: Ofer with persons
grammar_inventory.description: Two bounded accusative frames: gōd ofer persons, kind toward; nis ofer a teacher, not above in rank. In29.8 bare strong accusative plural ungeðancfulle/yfele denote unthankful/evil people; this exact personal-object use is newly taught here and is not inherited from prior bare genitive plural or article+weak adjective syntax. Neither ofer frame is a spatial crossing.

grammar_inventory.title: Swear by
grammar_inventory.description: Swęrian with ðurh+accusative names the oath standard. Repeated ne ðurh phrases share the initial negative command.

grammar_inventory.title: For in reciprocal replacement
grammar_inventory.description: For+dative in eye for eye/tooth for tooth expresses equivalent exchange. The first noun is nominative in the quoted formula.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: For+dative in eye for eye/tooth for tooth expresses equivalent exchange. The first noun is nominative in the quoted formula.

grammar_inventory.title: Teach people or a thing
grammar_inventory.description: Lǣran takes the taught people or taught matter as accusative object in these clauses. Passive teaching plus controlled infinitive remains supplied31.3.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Lǣran takes the taught people or taught matter as accusative object in these clauses. Passive teaching plus controlled infinitive remains supplied31.3.

grammar_inventory.title: Deliver from
grammar_inventory.description: Ālīes takes an accusative person; fram+dative names what the person is released from. Yfele is abstract substantive neuter dative.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Ālīes takes an accusative person; fram+dative names what the person is released from. Yfele is abstract substantive neuter dative.

grammar_inventory.title: A hundredfold requital
grammar_inventory.description: Use him mid hundtēontigum forgolden bið, “he will be repaid a hundredfold,” with the finite verb last. The initial ǣlc has its own relative clause and is resumed by dative him; this is an impersonal recipient-passive scaffold. Mid hundtēontigum is taken from the checked Duties paragraph, then adapted to this passive. For mīnum naman means for the sake of my name. Neither the numeral phrase nor this resumed construction is a new general production system.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: The ninth hour
grammar_inventory.description: Use nigoðan, the feminine accusative singular weak form of ninth, with tīd. The sixth-hour form siextan is already taught.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: The eleventh hour
grammar_inventory.description: Use ðā endleftan tīd for the eleventh hour. Endlefta follows Cook’s selected numeral spelling; this exact inflection is supplied.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Evening and a speech addressee
grammar_inventory.description: Use ðā hit ǣfen geworden wæs, when it had become evening. Geworden is supplied from geweorðan; do not manufacture a new full system. Cweðan tō his gerēfan names the person addressed, with tō+dative.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: In the heat
grammar_inventory.description: On ðisses dæges hǣte means in this day’s heat: on+dative gives the circumstance, while the day is an independent genitive.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Through him
grammar_inventory.description: The printed spelling ðurh is supplied beside previously taught þurh. Here ðurh hine means through/by way of him. The negation rejects the condemning purpose and contrasts it with saving; it does not deny that the Son was sent.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Of the Highest
grammar_inventory.description: Use ðæs Hēahstan as a masculine genitive singular divine title, of the Highest. This exact superlative title is supplied; the entire unused hēah comparison series is not assigned.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Swearing by a named standard
grammar_inventory.description: Use the exact spelling ðurh before the accusative oath standard; it is the supplied spelling of the taught through preposition. Hierusalem is the supplied place-name object.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: The resumed subject and one of a set
grammar_inventory.description: Cook’s emphatic resumed sē is the supplied long-vowel nominative masculine singular. In ān of ðissum lǣstum bebodum, of+dative selects one from the set. The same long sē may be retained in30.6.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: In old times
grammar_inventory.description: On ealdum tīdum means in old times: temporal on takes the dative plural here. This exact supplied temporal expression is distinct from locating an object in a place.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Proceeds and an omitted infinitive
grammar_inventory.description: Use æt his gewinne for from his labour. In ðæt hē mæg, what he can, a recoverable action such as obtain is left unexpressed. Cook159–161’s argument supplies the actual æt…gewinne…mæge construction; do not add a new independent ellipsis rule or infer a full gewinn paradigm.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Let them live
grammar_inventory.description: Use lǣt hīe libban, let them live: the accusative hīe is the understood subject of libban. This whole permission construction is scaffolded. Gif hīe magon expresses ability, not unwillingness; a defensible third-person optative translation is also valid language.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: A person taught to do something
grammar_inventory.description: Use hē wæs lǣred … tō dōnne. The taught person is the subject of the passive and the understood agent of doing. The infinitive’s object Godes willan stays accusative, with Godes genitive. This controlled infinitive frame is supplied.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: From evil
grammar_inventory.description: Use fram yfele, from evil. Here yfele is the dative singular of the substantive noun yfel (Cook’s noun§47 entry), not the ordinary adjective dative yfelum; the exact phrase is supplied.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: May it come about
grammar_inventory.description: Use Geweorðe first, as Cook specifies: it is the supplied third-singular present subjunctive of the prefixed verb. Swā-swā means just as; retain the supplied hyphenated source expression.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Names and the glossary Latin spelling
grammar_inventory.description: The proper names Ælfred, Osburg, Æthelwulf and Asser are supplied; Ælfredes is the genitive needed in31.14. Lǣdene follows the selected glossary’s Lǣden; the actual Preface reading retains its printed Lædene without a long mark. No silent change to that source reading is made.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Hight
grammar_inventory.description: Hātte means is/was called, with past time supplied by the context. It is a special passive naming form, not the ordinary active preterite hēt. Use it unchanged in this supported sentence.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: Fifty-two years
grammar_inventory.description: Use twā and fīftig gēara. The already taught two is combined with supplied fīftig; the numeral expression may govern genitive plural gēara. This one number phrase is supplied, not the full higher-numeral system.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: After twelve years of age
grammar_inventory.description: Use æfter ðǣm ðe … wæs for after he was…. In twęlf wintra eald, twelve years old, wintra is genitive plural with the numeral and adjective of age. This finite after-clause and age phrase are supplied; twęlf preserves the earlier selected form.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

grammar_inventory.title: A promise to whichever son
grammar_inventory.description: Use Engliscra lēoða, of English poems. The supported recipient expression is swā hwæðrum hiere twēgra suna swā hīe ǣrest leornode. Hwæðrum is dative singular because the whole expression is the recipient of promising, while its understood referent is the learner in the subordinate clause. This case attraction is supplied, not a general production target. Leornode here is prospective preterite subjunctive, identical in spelling to the indicative; it does not claim that he had already learned the book. Original independent free-choice exercises use nominative hwæðer and an explicit resumptive dative.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact local help; do not assess unsupported independent recall.

U03-ADJ-USE.evidence_note: Strong/weak conditions and agreement. Cook says weak sometimes after possessives; this is not a universal possessive→weak rule.

U03-STRONG.evidence_note: Complete strong pattern, short/long stems, æ/a alternation, disyllabic syncope and optional loss of -u, -e stems, h-loss and consonant simplification.

U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.
U03-THAN.edition: R. D. Fulk, An Introductory Grammar of Old English (2014), corrected open-access reprint, June 2020.
U03-THAN.source_attribution: Beo 469 in Fulk §35. Retain Fulk’s printed betere in this evidence quotation; it is not the selected masculine comparative model in the course.

U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.claim: The entry distinguishes uninflected participles from inflected and mixed usage with habban. The object may be described by an accusative participle; the finite auxiliary still agrees with its subject. Bare and agreeing realizations are evidenced alternatives, not an exceptionless mapping from English perfect grammar.

exact_examples.analysis: Plural finite subject Hie contrasts with singular accusative hine/ofslægenne. This is evidence for object-linked participial inflection, not participle agreement with the finite subject.

exact_examples.text: Ðú hafast helle bereáfod and ðæs deáþes aldor gebundenne
exact_examples.analysis: The coordinated example combines a bare participle with an inflected accusative-masculine participle referring to the object aldor.

U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.evidence_limits: Use the selected bare bases for Unit12 production. Recognize or accept appropriately agreeing alternatives only where their actual inflection and lexical use are supported. These evidence examples are not added learner tasks, vocabulary assignments or assigned source reading. No general causative or every historical perfect use is introduced.

authoring_rules: Preserve all original Cook words, hints, references, controls, group/exercise/item IDs and complete sets. Modern directions/help are separate.

Print every complete assigned matrix literally with rules, stems, important alternatives and sense/number limits. Distinguish logical positions, actual forms, multiword construction components and explicitly unassigned slots.
Teach all required independent forms, senses and uses before their first example/practice. Every supplied expression has visible support throughout its task; exposure is not unaided recall.
Retain all415 exact reading words,27 original notes and33 anchors. Duties is an opening argument, not a whole speech. Source punctuation and source questions remain identifiable apparatus.
Eight translated examples and55 original tasks are new teaching material. The three source passages supply the connected graded readings; no separate new narrative is assigned.
Keep the answer key separate and cover every requested output with meaning, target, explanation, alternatives and useful diagnosis. Distinguish grammatical validity from a stated source target.

A fresh non-author freezes all actual learner solutions in Git before explicit current-key/contract/audit/model comparison access. A separate fresh reviewer checks all complete paradigms, primary evidence and scope.

Resolve material findings; export complete learner/key PDFs, check full content parity and have non-authors inspect every final page. Preserve earlier records/artifacts, update indexes, export Beads and commit locally. Do not draft Unit16.

review_independence_protocol.main_reviewer: Fresh non-author to be assigned after complete drafts
review_independence_protocol.blind_phase: Solve every actual learner task from student.md and its visible teaching and support. Earlier accepted learner chapters and actual fourteen-unit registers may be consulted. Initial allowlist: the current learner master, accepted earlier learner materials/registers, original primary images or scans without current editorial annotation, AGENTS.md, EDITORIAL_POLICY.md and this neutral protocol. Do not open the current coverage contract, brief, audits, proposals, source token maps, key, ordered models, complete translation witnesses or helpers exposing them. An audit filename need not say private to contain answers.
review_independence_protocol.freeze_gate: Coordinator verifies every actual requested output is attempted, records learner identity, exports Beads and commits the unchanged witness locally. Only the coordinator's subsequent explicit message unlocks comparison. Elapsed time or files appearing do not unlock it.
review_independence_protocol.comparison_phase: Compare every frozen solution with the separate key, actual requested output positions, target versus validity distinctions, evidence and exact assigned dependencies. Keep the initial witness immutable; record corrections and disagreements separately. Resolve all material findings and bind acceptance to final actual masters and substantive contract identity.
review_independence_protocol.paradigm_reviewer: Separate fresh non-author agent: inspect all complete actual displays, diagnostics and derivations against primary evidence, accounting for each cell and the negation, quantity and comparison scope rules. Structural equality alone is not linguistic proof.
review_independence_protocol.exclusive_files: Reviewers edit only their allocated review files; the coordinator owns contract and integration, and authors own lesson/key repairs.
review_independence_protocol.known_exposure: Root, unit15_source, unit15_grammar and unit15_design have current audit or design roles and are ineligible to claim a fresh blind solve of this unit.
review_independence_protocol.page_review: Every final learner/key page requires non-author visual inspection, bound to final PDF and rendered-image identities. Byte-identical reuse must identify the actual earlier inspected image; hashing alone is not inspection.

This avoids an unevidenced multiplicative spelling and does not promote a general higher-number system. Cook's English prompt has no contrary Old English lexical control.

lexical_frames.construction: Onfōn can take an accusative material payment, as the directly attested onféngon hig syndrige penegas (Mt20.10). Teach this bounded frame for pęning and māre; the Unit14 dative-receive frame remains valid.
Dōn takes an accusative object and an agreeing predicate gelīc; the comparison person is dative. Direct source Þū dydest hig gelīce ūs (Mt20.12) supports hīe ūs gelīce.
Wið+dative expresses payment/return: wið his dæges weorce; wið ānum pęninge. This is distinct from the prior hostile combat use.
Forgieldan: recipient dative, paid thing accusative. A passive with retained recipient dative is locally scaffolded in28.1.
Wēnan introduces a ðæt-content clause. In this past report sceolden expresses what the workers expected to receive; it is not automatically an obligation.
Eall can strengthen the equative: eall swā micel swā, just as much as. Micel is substantive neuter; the second recipient remains dative under the understood giving verb.

Two bounded accusative frames: gōd ofer persons, kind toward; nis ofer a teacher, not above in rank. In29.8 bare strong accusative plural ungeðancfulle/yfele denote unthankful/evil people; this exact personal-object use is newly taught here and is not inherited from prior bare genitive plural or article+weak adjective syntax. Neither ofer frame is a spatial crossing.
Swęrian with ðurh+accusative names the oath standard. Repeated ne ðurh phrases share the initial negative command.
For+dative in eye for eye/tooth for tooth expresses equivalent exchange. The first noun is nominative in the quoted formula.
Lǣran takes the taught people or taught matter as accusative object in these clauses. Passive teaching plus controlled infinitive remains supplied31.3.
Ālīes takes an accusative person; fram+dative names what the person is released from. Yfele is abstract substantive neuter dative.
